heading: What `regex: false` is not
text:
### What `regex: false` is not [LNRE.1.3]

- Not a performance dial. Regex evaluation under RE2 is already
  bounded-cost ([LREG.9.3]); `regex: false` removes no timing term and is
  not a `linear_scan: false`-style algorithmic-shape constraint.
- Not implied by `linear_scan: false` or `realtime`. `linear_scan: false` bounds a
  regex match's cost ([LNLS.3.7]) but does not forbid regex;
  `realtime` enforces that same bound automatically ([LNLS.2.3]) but
  likewise does not forbid regex. Both may combine with `regex: false`,
  which forbids it outright.
- Not required for a regex-free program to run on a regex-less runtime.
  The load-time check in [LNRE.4.2] follows the artefact's content, not
  its settings, so a program that never writes a regex loads on such a
  runtime whatever its `regex` setting. Setting it moves the same
  guarantee earlier, to compile time, and turns a future regex addition
  into an immediate compile error instead of a deploy-time surprise.
- Not a special mechanism. It is one capability setting among the
  others ([LCAP.1]), refused like any other with
  `DS_VALIDATE_CAPABILITY_DISABLED`; it introduces no error code and no
  runtime behavior of its own.
